title: Human studies of ergothioneine | Surface Your Real Self
abstract: The third graphic for Ergothioneine dosing, Part 2 showed a human study where a 25 mg dosing stopped after Day 7, but the plasma ergothioneine level stayed significantly higher than baseline through Day 35. > *“We conducted an 8-week, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial to evaluate effects of daily oral supplementation with 30 mg of ergothioneine (DR.ERGO®) on skin parameters in healthy adult women aged 35–59 years who reported subjective signs of skin aging. A study investigated associations of plasma ergothioneine levels and cognitive changes in older adults over a two-year period:. > *“Observational studies have found that lower plasma levels of ergothioneine (ET) are significantly associated with higher risks of neurodegenerative diseases. Since the first trial’s participants showed slightly above-average cognitive function (neurocognitive index median = 105), with plasma ergothioneine levels of median = 1154 nM at baseline, and this study showed plateauing effects above 1000 ng/mL, I wonder how raising plasma ergothioneine levels above 1000 ng/mL could possibly show a net benefit for older people?
